why: Classic graph m-coloring: assign colors to vertices 0..n-1 in order, trying each color that no already-colored neighbour uses, and undo on failure. With n <= 12 the backtracking search is small, especially when you break the symmetry between unused colors.
hints: Color vertices one at a time. What must be true of a color before you give it to the next vertex?
A color is legal for vertex u if no neighbour of u already has it. Recurse to u + 1; if it fails, try the next color, and if none works, backtrack.

Build adjacency sets (dedupe repeated edges, reject self-loops immediately). Only try colors 0..(colors used so far), since any brand-new color is interchangeable with every other new one. Worst case O(m^n) but tiny here.
pitfalls: A self-loop makes coloring impossible regardless of m.
Repeated edges are allowed; they should not break anything.
Disconnected vertices still need a color, but any color works for them.
